severity_rationale: Meets C4 Medium criteria: 'value leak with stated assumptions and external requirements.' Every emergencyWithdraw with non-zero accrued pending permanently strands phUSD tokens that are already debited from rewardBudget, credited to accRewardPerShare, but owed to no one after the user's stake is zeroed. The conservation invariant (balance == rewardBudget + totalDebt) is permanently broken. Stated assumption: user has non-zero pending accrual at time of emergency exit. External requirement: an emergency-exit event occurs (pause, hook breakage, or user panic — all anticipated by design). The forfeiture itself is spec-blessed (masterchef-style), but the downstream stranding (tokens neither recoverable by owner nor redistributable to remaining stakers) is not explicitly blessed and represents a real value leak per exit event, accumulating over a long-lived pool. Not High because no direct theft path exists — the tokens are locked, not stolen. Not Low because each event produces non-dust stranding and the design explicitly anticipates multiple emergency exits.
title: emergencyWithdraw permanently strands forfeited rewards as dead tokens in the contract
description: When a staker calls emergencyWithdraw, _updatePool is deliberately not called (the escape hatch). At that moment, the staker's accrued pending reward (user.amount * accRewardPerShare / ACC_PRECISION - user.rewardDebt at last settlement) has already been debited from rewardBudget and credited to accRewardPerShare in earlier _updatePool calls. The phUSD tokens backing that accrual are therefore sitting in rewardToken.balanceOf(contract) but outside rewardBudget. When the user exits, their claim is silently erased (user.amount = 0; user.rewardDebt = 0). accRewardPerShare is not rewound, so other stakers' pending is unchanged — they earn their own shares, not the forfeited one. The tokens remain in the contract but are owed to no one: rewardBudget has already been decremented for them, so subsequent schedule resets don't touch them, and no owner rescue path exists.
attack_path: 1) Alice stakes 10 units. Bob stakes 10 units. Schedule runs. 2) 100 seconds pass. _updatePool credits 100*rate in accrual to accRewardPerShare; rewardBudget decrements by 100*rate. Alice and Bob each have pending = 50*rate. The 100*rate of phUSD is in the contract balance (outside rewardBudget). 3) Alice panics and calls emergencyWithdraw. user.amount = 0, rewardDebt = 0. The 50*rate of phUSD that backed her pending is still in contract balance, but no one is owed it anymore. 4) Bob eventually claims his 50*rate. Invariant `balance == rewardBudget + totalDebt` now has a persistent 50*rate gap: the contract holds 50*rate more than anyone is owed. Permanently lost.
impact: Every emergencyWithdraw silently burns the caller's already-debited accrual into permanently dead funds. Not recoverable by the exiting user (forfeiture is the design) but also not redistributed to remaining stakers and not reclaimable by the owner. The design explicitly anticipates multiple emergency exits (pause + ID migration, broken-hook scenarios), so accumulation into meaningfully stranded phUSD is expected over a long-lived pool. Conservation invariant (balance == rewardBudget + totalDebt) is permanently broken after any emergencyWithdraw with non-zero accrued pending.
recommendation: Three options, ranked: (a) On emergencyWithdraw, rewind the user's debited accrual back into rewardBudget (computed as user.amount * accRewardPerShare / ACC_PRECISION - user.rewardDebt) before zeroing out their stake — this rolls forfeited rewards into future emissions without touching accRewardPerShare, preserving the 'never trigger pool updates' property of the escape hatch. (b) Add an owner-only rescueDust function that sweeps balance - rewardBudget - liveTotalDebt. (c) Document the stranding as intentional and accept the conservation break.

sanitization.rationale: Root cause is emergencyWithdraw implementation in NFTStaker.sol. The user-forfeits-pending behavior IS spec-stated, but the conservation-invariant break (tokens stranded with no owner) is NOT explicitly blessed in CLAUDE.md and is a consequence rather than a stated design goal. Flagged for human review because standard masterchef forks show the same behavior; a judge may treat it as intentional. Severity may be downgraded by classifier.
